correctness.rationale: The commutator matrix is derived entrywise from UT_3(R), with the free central scalar contributing q^2. Rank 0/1/2/3 residue types are disjoint and exhaustive; the rank-two support is the three given threefolds. Elementary row-column reduction over dual numbers proves rank_k(M)=2rank(M_0)+rank(K). For rank-one residues the residual two-by-three matrix has exactly three computed rank frequencies. For rank-two residues Jacobian gradients of explicit 3x3 minors have ranks nu=2 at 3q^2(q-1) residues and nu=1 at 2q(q-1), giving exact q^(5-nu) vanishing-lift counts. Expanded frequencies sum to q^12 and yield the displayed commuting probability by centralizer averaging. A standalone direct Gaussian-elimination checker exhaustively verifies every k-valued parameter set for q=2 and q=3, including the individual seven frequencies. Finite enumeration is corroboration, not the proof for all q.

value.rationale: The object is the first nontrivial triangular algebra over a first-order local thickening where consecutive off-diagonal products couple. The entire centralizer-size distribution, not merely one commuting probability, is a natural ring invariant. Three determinantal components and their singular intersections explain why generic and exceptional dual lifts contribute different ranks; this is not a routine field substitution or a lone extra computed point. The exact formula applies uniformly to every finite field, and the explicit lifting mechanism is reusable in related finite local algebra calculations.
